clue.text: Little tyke Beverly Hills cops shot from behind

indicators.note: coming at a word from behind means starting at its far end, so its letters are read the other way along the row

parts.note: the LAPD is the Los Angeles Police Department, the force of the city Beverly Hills is surrounded by
a shot at something is a go at it, and this go is written the other way round

explanation.walkthrough: A tyke is also a naughty child, which is the reading the surface wants you to take. Filbert's police force comes straight off a cinema poster and hands over four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyke is an old word for a dog, usually a small mongrel, so a little tyke is the pet breed small enough to sit on a lap.

clue.text: African bug left, because harmless? Not quite so

indicators.note: a word given not quite in full stops short of its end, so the last letter never gets written down

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left, as in a stage direction
as it was raining and because it was raining say the same thing
something harmless is safe to handle, eat or say
so tired means very tired, and the word arrives one letter short

explanation.walkthrough: 'Harmless? Not quite so' reads as somebody correcting themselves about a danger. It is really two of the four pieces, plus the instruction that trims the last of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is the viral illness spread by rats in West Africa, and bug is the everyday word for an infection you catch.

clue.text: Press engagement quiet band keeps to

parts.note: p is the musician's mark for piano, the instruction to play softly

indicators.note: a band that keeps something has it held within it, so the letters named next go inside the ring rather than after it

parts.note: a hoop is a band of wood or metal, round a barrel or a skirt
the little word is taken at face value and hands over both its letters

explanation.walkthrough: 'Press engagement quiet' reads as a hush falling over a newsroom. Filbert's band is not the kind that plays, and the smallest word in the clue is doing real letter work.
explanation.definitionFit: A photo op is the staged appointment a public figure turns up to purely to be photographed, which is an engagement laid on for the press.

clue.text: Public touching not the done thing

parts.note: a secret made public is out, and a person who is out has declared themselves openly
re means concerning: a memo touching on expenses is a memo re expenses

explanation.walkthrough: Two everyday words sit end to end with nothing to signal the join. French spells it with an accent on the E; the grid, like most English writing, drops it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre means so far outside accepted taste that it startles people, which is what anyone means by saying a thing simply is not done.

clue.text: Scotch back in barrels which the drink escapes from?

definitions.note: The definition is a relative clause with no noun in front of it: the head it needs, something like 'the openings', is left for you to supply, because the surface's 'barrels' is busy doing wordplay.

parts.note: to scotch a rumour and to scupper a plan are the same move: both stop it dead

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter, and 'in' says to look inside the word that follows for it, so only that one letter is taken

parts.note: only the rearmost letter of the word is wanted, and that is an S

explanation.walkthrough: Barrels are what drink escapes from in the surface, and sailors call the sea the drink. The word itself is not a container here: it gives up one letter and no more.
explanation.definitionFit: Scuppers are the holes along a ship's deck edge that let water run back out to sea, so the sea is what escapes through them.

clue.text: Infer fraud's honest

parts.note: a con is a swindle, and the apostrophe s of the surface hands over the fourth letter
a true friend is an honest one, not pretending to be anything else

explanation.walkthrough: Three words, no indicator and no joining word: the first is the definition and everything after it is spelling. The possessive belongs to the wordplay, not to the grammar.
explanation.definitionFit: To construe a remark is to take it as meaning something, which is what you do when you infer a meaning from what was said.

clue.text: Artiste first noted after agent given raise

indicators.note: to note a thing is to write it down, and writing it after what is already there puts it second in the assembly
this is a down entry, so a piece given a raise is read back up the column and its letters come out in the opposite order

parts.note: an agent who acts for you is your rep, and that rep is then read back up the column
the former of two things is the first one mentioned

explanation.walkthrough: The surface has an agent winning a client a pay rise, and none of it survives. 'First' is the adjective for the earlier of two, not the front of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A performer is anybody who does a turn in front of an audience, and artiste is the slightly grander word for exactly that person.

clue.text: At any time, cryptic set difficult challenge

indicators.note: something cryptic has had its sense hidden, and letters hide their sense by not standing in the order you expect

parts.note: if you have ever done it, you have done it at any time at all
the three letters of the word arrive in a different order

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cryptic set' looks like a compiler at work on a grid, and is really an instruction with its three letters attached. The definition is a mountain used as a measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the peak everything else is measured against, so its name stands for the hardest test a person can take on.

clue.text: Comb for long-haired adherent caught

indicators.note: if you did not catch what somebody said you did not hear it, so this word asks for the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a Sikh follows the religion founded in the Punjab, whose members leave their hair uncut, and the name is said this way

explanation.walkthrough: 'Long-haired adherent' is a straight description rather than a joke, and the whole mechanism is in the ear: one sound with two quite different spellings.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb an area for something is to search it inch by inch, and that hunting is what the answer means as a verb.

clue.text: Republican in Troon, his new golf club

indicators.note: a set of letters made new is not the set you were handed, because the order it comes back in is not the one it went in with

parts.note: R is the standard abbreviation for a member of the American party
eight more letters for the mix, and Troon is the Ayrshire town whose links host the Open

explanation.walkthrough: Royal Troon has held the Open ten times, so the surface reads as a story about a course and a player. Count the letters against the (5,4) and it turns into raw material.
explanation.definitionFit: The short irons are the high-numbered clubs a golfer picks for approach shots, so the answer names one particular kind of club.

clue.text: Drive off without parking to keep looping around

indicators.note: a word that goes without something no longer has it, so the letter named next comes out of the longer word

parts.note: to repel an attacker is to drive them off
P is the letter on the road sign for a car park, and it is the letter that leaves

explanation.walkthrough: Every word of the surface belongs to a car: drive off, parking, looping around. Only the last three are the definition, and the rest is one word losing a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to whirl round and round on and on, the way a line runs off a fishing drum, so continuous looping is the sense.

clue.text: Female ruff's beak

definitions.meaning: the ornithological sense: the ruff is a wading bird whose male grows a collar of feathers in spring, and the hen has her own name
the slang sense: in British usage the beak is the magistrate you are hauled up in front of

explanation.walkthrough: Two definitions with only an apostrophe holding them together, and the surface pretends a bird has a bill. The word lives on in Canada, where a reeve chairs a rural council.
explanation.definitionFit: The hen of the ruff, a wading bird, is a reeve, and a reeve was also a local magistrate, which is what British slang means by beak.

clue.text: Area supervisors note ID with alterations written above

indicators.note: letters that come with alterations do not come as they were given, so this pair of words is remade into another order

parts.note: A is the standard abbreviation for area, in a formula or on a plan
the foremen on a site are the workers who supervise the rest of it
six letters remade from the two short words

explanation.walkthrough: Fourteen letters and only six of them shuffle, so the count is the way in: the first eight are handed over straight. Two small words carry the whole of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something aforementioned has already been named earlier on the page, which in a document means written above the point you have reached.

clue.text: See incomplete clone, taking copy exactly

indicators.note: a word left incomplete is a letter short, and the letter it goes without is the one at the end

parts.note: the word arrives one letter short, its final E left off

indicators.note: a word taking something has it in its keeping, so what follows goes inside rather than after

parts.note: to ape somebody is to copy their manner
agreeing with somebody by saying exactly is agreeing by saying yes

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a laboratory story about a half-grown clone, and every word of it is doing letter work instead. 'Exactly' is the agreeing exclamation, not the adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap eyes on somebody is to catch sight of them, the idiom English keeps for seeing a person for the first time in a while.

clue.text: Cautionary rating on English wine to send to France?

indicators.note: 'on' is doing the loose job of 'next to' here: in an across entry it sets the rating alongside the letter named, which means after it

parts.note: E is the usual abbreviation for English, as on a school timetable
X was the British film certificate that barred anyone under sixteen, the warning label of its day
port is the fortified wine of the Douro, drunk after dinner

explanation.walkthrough: The X certificate was retired in 1982, replaced by the 18. 'Cautionary rating' points at that piece of British cinema history rather than at anything a wine merchant would say.
explanation.definitionFit: To export is to send goods out of the country, and France is only one place you might send them, which is what the question mark admits.

clue.text: Harry looked at text from Spooner, Charles's old foe

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner was famous for exchanging the opening sounds of two words, so you say the pair with their first sounds swapped over

parts.note: to harry somebody is to hound them, chasing and pestering without let-up
looking at text is reading it

parts.words: Harry looked at text from Spooner
parts.note: swap the sounds the two words start with and the pair comes out as the grid entry

explanation.walkthrough: Two ordinary verbs, and the man supplying the instruction was an Oxford don whose slips of the tongue became a noun. Note the capital H: it is misdirection, not a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roundheads were the parliamentary soldiers who fought Charles I in the Civil War, named for the cropped hair of the apprentices who backed them.

clue.text: Unsatisfied girl has bagged bronze for shooting

indicators.note: to bag a thing is to put it in a bag, and a word that has bagged another has it shut up inside itself

parts.note: gal is the informal spelling of the way some speakers say the word
a demand nobody has satisfied is an unmet one

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bronze for shooting' wants to be an Olympic medal in the pistol event, and that is the trap: it is a metal here, not a placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunmetal is the tough copper, tin and zinc bronze that cannon used to be cast from, so the alloy is named for the shooting it was made for.

clue.text: One staying out later, probably after 12?

definitions.text: One staying out later, probably after 12?

parts.note: the reading the surface pushes: somebody out past midnight, later than the hour the rest of the clue seems about to name
the reading meant: 12 is an age, not an hour, and the years that come after it are the ones being counted

explanation.walkthrough: Everything turns on what 12 is. Read as a clock it makes the clue a curfew story; read as an age it is the boundary the answer begins at, and 'later' means later than they used to.
explanation.definitionFit: A teenager is anybody aged thirteen to nineteen, so those years do begin just after twelve, and the later nights out are what parents notice first.

clue.text: Did champion model speedos around university?

indicators.note: to model clay is to work it into another shape, and letters worked into another shape do not keep the order they came in
what goes around something is inside it, so the university's letter is posted in among the others rather than parked at an end

parts.note: seven letters for the mix, taken from the trunks the surface is wearing
U is the standard abbreviation for university

explanation.walkthrough: 'Did champion' is the definition and reads as a boast about a swimmer's record. Count the letters of the trunks against the (8) and the U has to be joining them.
explanation.definitionFit: To espouse a cause is to take it up and argue for it, which is what championing a cause means, and both are in the past tense.

clue.text: Poor worker nice giving away pound

indicators.note: what you give away you no longer have, so the letter named next leaves the word it was sitting in

parts.note: a nice afternoon is a pleasant one
the pound sign is a curly capital L, from the Latin libra

explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor worker' looks like a judgement on somebody's effort and is really a description of their station: the word names a rank in the old land system.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a smallholder or farm labourer at the bottom of that system, so the word carries the work and the poverty together.

clue.text: Contract groom listened to in court

indicators.note: a word listened to reaches you as a sound, so you write down what the ear gets rather than what the dictionary prints

parts.note: a bird grooming its feathers is preening, and that sound opens the answer with a spelling of its own
somebody appearing before a magistrate is up in court, or up before the beak

explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a bridegroom giving evidence, and neither half of it survives: one is a bird tidying its feathers, the other the idiom for standing before a magistrate.
explanation.definitionFit: A prenup is the agreement a couple sign before marrying to settle who owns what if it ends, and that is a contract.

clue.text: Removing eggs, e.g. nits spread after November

indicators.note: letters spread out are letters no longer stacked in the order they were given, so they resettle in another one
the shuffled letters are written after the letter November stands for, not in front of it

parts.note: November is the international radio alphabet's word for N
six letters for the mix, the two of the abbreviation among them

explanation.walkthrough: 'E.g.' looks like it is introducing an example and is not: its two letters are fodder like any others, which is the hardest thing to spot here.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting is the old country pastime of hunting out birds' nests and taking the eggs from them, which is why it is now illegal.

clue.text: Knock black and blue

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, on a pencil and on a chess scoresheet
somebody feeling blue is feeling low, and both mean downhearted

explanation.walkthrough: 'Black and blue' is the phrase for bruised, which is what a knock leaves behind, so the surface and the definition tell one story in two vocabularies.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow is a single knock or stroke delivered by hand or weapon, and both words are the noun for the impact itself.

clue.text: Lord Chancellor is wary called on mobile

indicators.note: a mobile thing is free to move, and letters free to move will not stay in the places the clue put them

parts.note: fourteen letters, the whole middle of the clue going into the mix

explanation.walkthrough: The surface is a phone call to a nervous minister, and one word at the end turns all of it into raw material. Count the letters against the (8,6) before starting.
explanation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Wolsey held the Lord Chancellorship under Henry VIII, so the office is named and the man who filled it is wanted.

clue.text: Cargo ship's steam generator failing to start

indicators.note: a word that fails to start never gets its opening letter down, so the first letter is the one dropped

parts.note: a boiler is what raises steam, in a ship's engine room or a house

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cargo ship's steam generator' reads as one item on a ship's inventory and is two things: the definition stops after the second word, and the rest is a word losing its head.
explanation.definitionFit: An oiler is a tanker, the cargo ship whose cargo is oil, and navies use the word for the vessel that refuels a fleet at sea.

clue.text: House with a lot of land, miles and miles

definitions.text: House with a lot of land

parts.note: somewhere miles away is somewhere far away, the distance measured loosely
m is the abbreviation printed on a road sign for the unit

explanation.walkthrough: One word does two different jobs in a row, which is the joke of the clue: the same four letters give a word for a long way and then a unit of measurement.
explanation.definitionFit: A farm is the whole working holding, house and buildings and the acres around them, so the definition names the dwelling together with its land.

clue.text: Saw time on notice

indicators.note: in an across entry a piece written on another sits alongside it, and the convention puts what is placed on second

parts.note: an ad in the paper is a notice placed there to be read
the age of steam is the time of steam, a stretch of history

explanation.walkthrough: 'Saw' is a noun here rather than the past tense of see, and that single switch is the whole difficulty of a three-word clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is an old maxim, the worn sort of saying quoted as wisdom, and an adage is that same handed-down proverb.

clue.text: With old Golf pulled over, people needing the AA vanish

indicators.note: a car pulled over is turned in off the road, and the letters before it are turned in the same way, to read the other way round

parts.note: Golf is G in the radio alphabet, old is O and with is W, and the three are then turned round
alkies are alcoholics, and the AA they need is Alcoholics Anonymous rather than the breakdown service

explanation.walkthrough: The Golf and the AA both belong to the road, and neither is doing motoring work: one is a letter of the radio alphabet, the other a fellowship of drinkers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has gone walkies has disappeared from where it was left, the jokey British way of saying an object has been mislaid or pinched.

clue.text: Bullfighter with no cojones a bit yellow, mother admits

indicators.note: a word that admits another lets it in, so what follows is placed inside those two letters rather than after them

parts.note: ma is the nursery word for a mother
a tad late and a bit late are the same amount of late
in heraldry or is gold, which on a shield is painted yellow

explanation.walkthrough: The rude aside is the definition: Spanish marks a female bullfighter by changing the ending, and cojones is Filbert's way of saying which ending is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Matadora is the feminine form of matador, so the bullfighter the clue wants is a woman, which is the point of the Spanish crudity.

clue.text: Doctor home after round where he started

indicators.note: the two pieces named in front of this word are written after the round one, so the circle leads and they follow it

parts.note: a round drawn on paper is the letter O
to doctor a result and to rig it are the same piece of cheating
somebody who is at home is in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' opens the clue like a title and is really the verb for tampering. The definition is the last three words, which read like a question and are not one.
explanation.definitionFit: An origin is the point something began from, a river's source or a person's birthplace, so where he started names it exactly.
